output.title: When definitions drift, start with one workflow
output.body:
If your team keeps using the same word three different ways, that is usually not a system problem yet. It is a workflow problem. The useful question is simple: which single recurring process shows signs that the same field, label, or category is being interpreted differently each time? In a small business, that could be invoices, customer records, handoffs, or email triage. Pick one. Do not try to tidy up the whole business in one sweep; that is how small problems become expensive hobbies.

Then count the drift instead of guessing it. For two weeks, track each time someone has to recategorise something, ask for clarification, fix a duplicate record, or redo an approval because the definition was unclear. Use actual instances, not a feeling that it is “a lot.” Once you can see where the rework sits, you can decide whether the next step is a clearer rule, a better template, or a grounded assistant that checks approved definitions in company documents before anything moves forward.

That fit check matters. If the task needs human judgment, policy sign-off, or context outside the written rule, AI is a helper, not a replacement. For money movement and other high-risk decisions, the owner still approves it. If code or workflow tooling is built, it should sit in the customer’s accounts from the start, with handover as policy rather than a promise of magic.
